newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia town hit by fresh riots, 18 injured.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia town hit by fresh riots, 18 injured.

text.p: Fresh political violence has flared in the town of Pekalongan on Indonesia's main Java island and at least 18 people were injured in fighting between rivals ahead of May 29 elections, residents said on Thursday.
They said supporters of the ruling Golkar party and the Moslem-oriented United Development Party (PPP) clashed in the town on Wednesday, and troops were called in to maintain order.
"Troops were deployed here last night to contain the riot. The town is tense today and many shops are closed because the owners are afraid of fresh violence," said one resident.

Police in Pekalongan declined comment. The town, on the coast in Central Java, has been the site of clashes since March between supporters of the PPP and Golkar, which seeks to push its share of votes above 70 percent after winning 68 percent in 1992.
Tensions have risen since the start last Sunday of the campaign for the May 29 general elections, and there have been minor clashes between Golkar and PPP supporters elsewhere in the country.
Meanwhile, the country's armed forces have asked the three political parties contesting the election to stop travelling in convoys, the Jakarta Post reported.

"The (leaders of the) contestants should persuade their supporters to stop travelling in convoys during this campaign," the newspaper quoted Armed Forces spokesman Brigadier-General Slamet Supriadi as saying.
Thousands of supporters of the PPP and Golkar staged illegal parades in Jakarta and other parts of Java island on Tuesday and Wednesday, causing traffic jams.
At least one PPP supporter was killed in a road accident in the East Java town of Pasuruan on Tuesday while taking part in a procession, newspapers have said.

Only Golkar, the PPP and the Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) are allowed to contest the election for the 425 elected seats in the House of Representatives. A further 75 seats are allotted to the military, which does not vote.
The government has banned parties from staging street rallies during the campaign to avoid clashes between supporters, but both the PPP and Golkar have largely ignored the directive.
Violence has been reported in several towns in Indonesia during the election campaign, which lasts through May 23.

The official Antara news agency said the PPP had cancelled a campaign meeting scheduled for Friday in the city of Yogyakarta in Central Java after a group of people smashed the windows of the party's office on Wednesday.
The agency said the PPP also cancelled a rally in Medan, North Sumatra, planned for Wednesday after three supporters were injured in a clash with Golkar backers on Saturday.

The PDI has also discontinued campaigning in Indonesia's second city Surabaya in East Java after about 5,000 supporters of the party's ousted leader, Megawati Sukarnoputri, stormed a gathering organised by the rival, government-backed faction.
The Media Indonesia newspaper reported that the PDI also decided not to stage rallies in Ujung Pandang, South Sulawesi, on Wednesday for fear of violence.
